title_yt: Is GTA 6 really expensive? Check the math #Shorts
title_fb: Is GTA 6 really expensive? Check the math
hook: Tomorrow, GTA 6 comes out. Benny pays about eighty dollars. The cashier calls it a bargain.
open_loop: Lines 1-2 picture a cashier calling an about-eighty-dollar game a bargain and Benny staggering; the 'why' (inflation-adjusted GTA 5 price) is withheld to lines 5-7.
payoff: GTA 5 cost $59.99 in Sept 2013, about $86 in today's money (CPI-U 234.149 to 337.511). GTA 6 Standard is $79.99, about $6 cheaper in real terms.

lines.visual: SCENE 1 (frame 0): Benny (money outfit, cash prop) beside a counter spot, excited, headline 'TOMORROW' already on screen, badge 'GTA 6' plain text; hooded stranger (cast, flip) as the cashier on the right. Snap-zoom on 'Tomorrow'.

lines.text: Benny pays about eighty dollars. The cashier calls it a bargain.
lines.visual: SCENE 2 (on 'pays'): Benny slaps cash on the counter (cash prop), badge '~$80' with a clink. SCENE 3 (on 'bargain'): the cashier points and grins (smug) with bubble 'BARGAIN!' (pop); GAG: Benny's jaw drops, he staggers back (thud), shock pose.

lines.text: Does that sound crazy to you?
lines.visual: SCENE 4: Benny points at the viewer on 'you', headline 'CRAZY?' on 'crazy'; GAG: coins rain (coins) and one bonks his head (thud), he spins with worry pose.

lines.text: Prices rise, so we compare in today's money.
lines.visual: SCENE 5 (on 'Prices'): Benny thinking, badge 'PRICES RISE' (pop). SCENE 6 (on 'today's'): headline 'TODAY'S MONEY' replaces the badge (never both at once beyond 4 words); Benny presents with a flourish.

lines.text: In 2013, GTA 5 cost about sixty dollars.
lines.say: In two thousand thirteen, GTA five cost about sixty dollars.
lines.visual: SCENE 7: Benny in everyday outfit shrugs (whoosh time-hop); badge '2013' and a counter to 60 with prefix '~$' (ding) on 'sixty'. GAG: the cashier hands him a cash prop, he smirks.

lines.text: That is about eighty-six dollars today.
lines.visual: SCENE 8: flash cut; the counter climbs from 60 to 86 with prefix '~$' (ding, drum), snap-zoom, Benny shocked, badge 'TODAY'; cashier smug.

lines.text: So the new game is about six dollars cheaper.
lines.visual: SCENE 9 (on 'So'): two bars, labels 'GTA 5' value_label '~$86' (red) and 'GTA 6' value_label '~$80' (green). On 'cheaper': stamp '~$6 CHEAPER' slams (thud), Benny flex, confetti.

lines.text: Worth it or too much? Comment A or B.
lines.visual: SCENE 10 (on 'Worth'): rows 'A: WORTH IT' and 'B: TOO MUCH' pop; Benny points at the viewer on 'Comment'; cashier shrugs. Rows only, no footer.
lines.on_screen: A: WORTH IT / B: TOO MUCH

facts_used.claim: GTA V launched Sept 2013 at US standard price $59.99 (about $86 adjusted to today's money using BLS CPI-U).

math_check: 59.99 x 337.511 / 234.149 = 86.47 -> 'about 86' (Sep 2026 CPI 336.940 gives 86.33, also about 86). 86.47 - 79.99 = 6.48 -> 'about 6'; on screen ~$86, ~$80, ~$6 using the same rounded figures (86 - 80 = 6). Voice 'about eighty/sixty/eighty-six/six' = screen '~$80/~$60/~$86/~$6'.

upload.title: Is GTA 6 really expensive? Check the math #Shorts
upload.description:
A cashier calls an $80 game a bargain. Is she right?
Worth it or too much? Comment A or B.
GTA 5 launched at $59.99 in September 2013, about $86 in today's money (BLS CPI-U). GTA 6 Standard is $79.99, about $6 less in real terms. Cheaper after inflation does not mean easy to afford.
Not financial advice. Sources: BLS CPI-U, GG Recon, GameLuster.
#gta6 #money #inflation #Shorts

changes_from_previous: PIVOT from the vacation study (weak, shrug reveal, could not honestly reach GTA) to a number reveal: GTA 5's $59.99 in 2013 is about $86 in today's money, so GTA 6 at $79.99 is about $6 cheaper in real terms. Hook now pictures a cashier calling the game a bargain (explicit referent: the price). Benny lives the story throughout (counter, bonk gag, time hop, cashier). Early 'you' in line 3; caveat 'compare in today's money' spoken before the twist; reveal stated plainly (line 7) before the A/B. 'Tomorrow' anchor, no 'tonight'. Only drawable assets (badges, headlines, stamps, bubble, counter, bars, coins, confetti, stranger cast, cash prop). All numbers rounded with 'about' in voice and '~' on screen (Rule A).
